counterexample_that_still_passes: Set .talk-stream{overflow:hidden}. Content still overflows so scrollHeight stays greater than clientHeight and the assertion passes while nothing can be scrolled at all. Same for overflow:clip and for a fixed-height element with no scroll mechanism.
corrected_behavioral_assertion: Dispatch a real wheel event over the transcript and require stream.scrollTop to increase from 0; then scroll to the end and require the last message to be inside the stream's visible box.

counterexample_that_still_passes: Asserts a declaration, not behaviour. If any other ancestor scrolls — .nur-shell, #page-talk, documentElement or body — the page still moves under the user while .nur-viewport reports 'hidden' and the assertion passes.
corrected_behavioral_assertion: After the wheel gesture require documentElement.scrollTop, body.scrollTop and every ancestor of the transcript to be unchanged from their pre-gesture values.

counterexample_that_still_passes: Geometry only. The composer passes while covered by another element, while visibility:hidden, while opacity:0, or while clipped by an ancestor's overflow:hidden — in every case the owner cannot use it.
corrected_behavioral_assertion: Require Playwright's toBeVisible() plus an elementFromPoint hit test at the send control's centre resolving to the control or its descendant, after the transcript has been scrolled.

counterexample_that_still_passes: Size without reachability. A 500px box with overflow:hidden and 11,000px of content passes this while most of the conversation is permanently unreachable.
corrected_behavioral_assertion: Replaced by the end-content-reachable assertion: scroll to the bottom and require the final message's box to intersect the transcript's client box.

counterexample_that_still_passes: A declaration, not a capability. overflow:auto on a zero-height or content-sized element passes while nothing ever scrolls.
corrected_behavioral_assertion: Covered by the wheel-and-scrollTop assertion above.

claim: the journal draft scrolls inside itself
counterexample_that_still_passes: Same defect as the transcript: a textarea with overflow:hidden still reports scrollHeight greater than clientHeight.
corrected_behavioral_assertion: Focus the textarea, press Control+End, and require field.scrollTop to have increased and the caret line to be within the visible box.

counterexample_that_still_passes: No counterexample — existence of a specific id is exactly the claim.

current_assertion: single 6-second sample asserted against a fixed ceiling
counterexample_that_still_passes: One sample. The suite already produced 75.2%, 72%, 70.8% and one failing spike across identical runs, so a single reading can pass or fail on noise rather than on cost.
corrected_behavioral_assertion: Five samples per surface; assert the median against the ceiling and report median, p95, worst and baseline. A single failing sample is reported, never re-run away.

current_assertion: logs frame timings; asserts only points >= 2000
counterexample_that_still_passes: Frame timings were already withdrawn as assertions because three identical runs gave 50.1ms, 66.7ms and 83.4ms — exact vsync multiples measuring harness throttling. The remaining point-count assertion is honest but proves population, not performance.
corrected_behavioral_assertion: Point count kept as a population check. Performance is asserted only in v8-cpu-budget with five samples.

claim: every route and viewport was captured
counterexample_that_still_passes: Counts rows the harness itself produced. A route that rendered an error page, or rendered nothing, still contributes a row and passes.
corrected_behavioral_assertion: Capture harness rather than a correctness oracle. Marked as measurement-only in the audit; no PASS claim about the product should cite it.

counterexample_that_still_passes: Same defect, and the run in fact aborted after 5 of 13 states while the assertion shape suggested completeness.
corrected_behavioral_assertion: Measurement-only. The audit already records that this run failed at the offline step.

claim: the end of the transcript is reachable
current_assertion: stream.scrollTop = stream.scrollHeight, then assert the last row is inside the stream box
counterexample_that_still_passes: Assigning scrollTop scrolls an element even when overflow is hidden, so the replacement carried the exact defect it was written to remove. It passed on the broken build.
corrected_behavioral_assertion: Wheel repeatedly until scrollTop stops changing, then require scrollTop to be at the true maximum and the end of the last message to be on screen.

claim: the end of the transcript is reachable
current_assertion: last row fully inside the scroller: lBox.top >= sBox.top - 6 && lBox.bottom <= sBox.bottom + 6
counterexample_that_still_passes: Unfalsifiable at small viewports rather than falsely passing: at 390x400 a single wrapped message is taller than the scroller, so no implementation can satisfy it. It failed a correct build.
corrected_behavioral_assertion: Require the gesture to reach the true scroll bottom and the bottom edge of the last message to be visible; do not require the whole message to fit.

claim: the end of the draft is reachable by keyboard
counterexample_that_still_passes: Measured 6433 of 6456: the browser scrolls the caret into view, which stops one padding-bottom short of the scroll bottom. The last line was on screen and the check still failed.
corrected_behavioral_assertion: Derive the tolerance from the field's own padding-bottom plus line-height for the keyboard claim, and assert the exact bottom separately via a wheel gesture.

claim: the measured build is the build under test
current_assertion: vite preview reused across runs with reuseExistingServer, no build-identity check
counterexample_that_still_passes: The served bundle predated the stylesheet under test: its polish sheet contained neither the holographic section nor the scroll fix. Every reading taken against it described code that was not in the build, in either direction.
corrected_behavioral_assertion: Grep the built bundle for a sentinel from the CSS under test before trusting any run, and rebuild from a clean dist when it is absent.

claim: a failing assertion means a scroll defect
counterexample_that_still_passes: The entry sheet intermittently swallows the first submit, so two of four viewports reported failure on a build whose scrolling was correct. A flake was indistinguishable from a product defect.
corrected_behavioral_assertion: Retry sign-in up to three times and only then fail, so the scroll assertions are the only thing the result can be attributed to.
